subject: Hosted API commit tiers — Pricing, DPA gating, and SOC2 evidence
messages:
From: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@atlascommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Question on commit tiers & SOC2 for Hosted API

Hi Marissa,

We’re evaluating Redwood’s Hosted API for a customer-facing chat and embedding pipeline. Before we get too far along with usage estimates, two quick questions: 

1) For a committed, usage-based arrangement (we’re looking at an approximate baseline of ~10B tokens/month), what is the structure of per-token discounts across commit tiers? Can you share an indicative table for 1B/5B/10B+ commitments?

2) Our legal/procurement team requires evidence of SOC2 and a signed DPA before finalizing any committed pricing. Does Redwood require a signed DPA and SOC2 evidence before offering commit-tier pricing, or can we sign the commit now and provide the SOC2 evidence within a short window post-sign?

Procurement will want the pricing to be explicit in the quote. Can you include a draft DPA and any SOC2 summary or attestation you can share?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Maria
Maria Gonzales
Head of Platform Partnerships
Atlas Commerce
[maria.gonzales@atlascommerce.com]

[Attachment: requirements_atlas_202602.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@atlascommerce.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlascommerce.com>
Date: 2026-02-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Question on commit tiers & SOC2 for Hosted API

Hi Maria — great to hear from you, and thanks for the clear questions. Quick answers up front, then details below: 

- Indicative commit tiers: attached (Pricing_Commit_Tiers.xlsx). Typical discounts scale from ~10% at 1B to ~25% at 10B+ compared to on-demand per-token rates; we can tailor banding by contract term and payment cadence.
- SOC2/DPA gating: our standard enterprise practice is to require an executed DPA prior to binding a contractual commit tier. For SOC2: we provide our SOC2 Type II summary and security pack (attached) to procurement/legal as part of the diligence. In practice we can agree on a provisional commit price in parallel with the DPA process, but binding commit pricing requires the signed DPA.

If procurement needs a formal quote that calls out the gating condition ("commit pricing contingent on executed DPA and receipt of SOC2 summary"), we can include that language. If Atlas requires a hard dependency (no commit price until DPA signed), we understand and can escalate.

I’ve attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, SOC2_Summary_Q4-2025.pdf, Pricing_Commit_Tiers.xlsx. 

Next steps I suggest: 1) I’ll loop in our legal and security for any DPA redlines and SOC2 questions; 2) We’ll prepare a formal quote that includes both the provisional price and the gating clause; 3) If acceptable, we can schedule a 30-min procurement call to run through the DPA redlines and timeline.

Would you be able to confirm the exact token baseline you expect (10B is a helpful starting point) and procurement’s target timeline to sign?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Pricing_Commit_Tiers.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-09T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Question on commit tiers & SOC2 for Hosted API — need review (Atlas Commerce, RDW-2026-ATC-57)

Fwding thread from Atlas Commerce (Maria). They are asking whether commit pricing requires a signed DPA and SOC2 evidence. Key asks: 10B tokens baseline, procurement wants the DPA and SOC2 before finalizing commit pricing.

Can you review: 
- Evelyn: any DPA redlines we should expect? Attached is Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf — primary points of negotiation usually are data residency, liability caps, and deletion timelines.
- Vivek: is the SOC2_Summary_Q4-2025.pdf sufficient for procurement, or do they need the full report or an auditor letter?
- Rishi/Ben: can we offer a provisional commit pricing approach (i.e., pricing reserved for 14 days while DPA is signed) or do we need to insist on signed DPA before prize locks?

Attachments included: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, SOC2_Summary_Q4-2025.pdf, Pricing_Commit_Tiers.xlsx

Proposed negotiable concession: provisional 20% discount for 10B commit contingent on DPA executed within 30 days; if not executed in 30 days revert to on-demand pricing. Want to check legal/security OK before proposing to customer.

Thanks — can you reply with redlines/comments by EOD tomorrow?

—Marissa

From: Procurement <procurement@atlascommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Maria Gonzales <maria.gonzales@atlascommerce.com>
Cc: legal@atlascommerce.com
Date: 2026-02-10T10:14:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Question on commit tiers & SOC2 for Hosted API

Marissa / Marisa (cc’d),

Thanks for the attachments and the quick response. A few clarifications from procurement/legal: 

1) Atlas policy: committed pricing requires an executed DPA and receipt of SOC2 Type II report summary and auditor attestation prior to signature. A provisional hold is acceptable for a short period, but we can’t accept language that allows pricing to be retroactively applied after the fact.

2) Please confirm Redwood’s standard turnaround for DPA redline review and whether Redwood can accept our standard data deletion clause (we’ll send that as an attachment in a separate email).

3) Final quote: we need an explicit line item that states the commit term (12 months), token baseline (10B/month), per-token commit rate, discount applied, and the gating condition ("Execution of DPA and delivery of SOC2 Type II summary required prior to effective date of committed pricing").

If Redwood can prepare the quote with the gating clause and provide a draft DPA that your legal team is willing to negotiate quickly, we can move to an internal approval loop. Procurement would prefer the DPA executed before purchase order issuance.

Regards,
Procurement Team
Atlas Commerce
[Attachment: atlas_data_deletion_clause.docx (to follow)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps & proposed concession for Atlas (RDW-2026-ATC-57)

Team — quick summary and recommended next steps after procurement reply: 

Summary:
- Opportunity: Atlas Commerce, target baseline 10B tokens/month, 12-month commit.
- Procurement insists on executed DPA + SOC2 Type II summary prior to the effective date of committed pricing.
- They’ve asked for a formal quote that includes the gating clause.

Recommended approach (seeking legal/security sign-off):
1) Prepare formal quote that includes clear gating language: "Commit pricing effective upon execution of the DPA and receipt of SOC2 Type II summary; until such time, standard on-demand rates apply."
2) Offer a conditional commercial concession to accelerate decision: hold the proposed commit pricing for 14 calendar days from quote issuance as a courtesy (non-binding) while DPA is finalized. If DPA executed within 30 days, commit pricing becomes binding from the agreed effective date; if not, revert to on-demand.
3) Legal: review Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf against Atlas redlines (they’ll send). Proposed fallback: accept reasonable deletion and liability language but require procurement to accept standard Redwood security controls and indemnities.
4) Security (Vivek): confirm SOC2_Summary_Q4-2025.pdf + auditor letter is sufficient; if atlas needs full report we’ll follow procurement escalation process.

Please reply with redlines or "approve" so I can draft the formal quote and loop in sales leadership if we need to concede further on pricing. I’d like to get the quote to Atlas by EOD Monday to keep momentum.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: Pricing_Commit_Tiers.xlsx (Excel)]
